video_title: Knicks vs Spurs NBA Finals Game 1 Breakdown & Game 2 Preview With Draymond Green & Tim Legler

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green names Karl-Anthony Towns the MVP of Game 1
quotes.excerpt: the MVP was Karl-Anthony Towns. And the reason the MVP was Karl-Anthony Towns is because he did it
quotes.quote: The MVP of Game 1, I know everybody is going to say, 'Yo, Jalen Brunson had 30 points,' that's great. Yes, Jalen Brunson did have 30 points and yes, Jalen Brunson did close the game out. However, the MVP was Karl-Anthony Towns. And the reason the MVP was Karl-Anthony Towns is because he did it on both ends of the floor. Defensively, he was incredible.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: Draymond Green criticizes Stefan Castle's defensive assignment on Jalen Brunson
quotes.excerpt: I was a bit disappointed that Stefan Castle wasn't guarding Jalen Brunson more. There was a lot of switching
quotes.quote: I was a bit disappointed that Stefan Castle wasn't guarding Jalen Brunson more. There was a lot of switching, especially with the job that Stefan Castle, and to me, early on in the start of the game, Stefan Castle wasn't really even Jalen Brunson's matchup, which to watch a guy guard the MVP of the NBA, back-to-back MVP of the NBA, as good as we've seen anyone guard him for seven straight games, and then you come out and you're playing against Jalen Brunson and you're not glued to that guy, that was a bit disappointing to me.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler analyzes the impact of Victor Wembanyama's benching in Game 1
quotes.excerpt: they took Victor Wembanyama out of the game with seven minutes left in the third quarter

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: They took Victor Wembanyama out of the game with seven minutes left in the third quarter. And it was an early break for him. And I was sitting there at the time thinking, 'That's early.' And they're up 13, so was Mitch Johnson thinking, 'Man, this might be a great time to buy us some extra minutes of rest because we might want him to go longer in the fourth?' And at that time, the Knicks, they scored two points in the first five minutes of the third quarter out of the locker room.

text_blocks.speaker: Draymond Green
text_blocks.text: I agree with you 1000%. It's, however, that's my worry because that is the Knicks' strength.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler on the Knicks' offensive execution and Victor Wembanyama
quotes.excerpt: they had the fewest points per possession on those screens than they have his entire career

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: Last night, in a game in which Victor Wembanyama set at least 20 on-ball screens, they had the fewest points per possession on those screens than they have his entire career since he's been in San Antonio. And I think it's because of what you're saying. Like he, it was bumper cars for him.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler on the Knicks' stoic demeanor after clinching the series
quotes.excerpt: that flight home, he said it was dead quiet. There was no celebration on that plane

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: He said when they clinched against the Cavs, that flight home, he said it was dead quiet. There was no celebration on that plane. And I thought that was interesting. Even Mike Breen was kind of surprised about that. And he said, 'Because we just don't feel like we've done anything yet.'

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler on Victor Wembanyama's growth and maturity
quotes.excerpt: he doesn't necessarily look much bigger, but he plays a lot stronger than he did

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: He doesn't necessarily look much bigger, but he plays a lot stronger than he did when he first came into the league. That's going to continue to improve. His understanding of different coverages that he's going to see. I still think there's a lot of growth for him as a passer. And I said it last night early in the broadcast, one of his first moves, he went into that spin and I don't remember who it was, one of the Knicks was in his lap when he came out of the spin and he turned the ball over. And I said, 'If I'm the Knicks, every single time he puts it down and he goes into a spin, someone needs to be there because the one thing he still isn't going to do yet is pick you apart with his passing.'

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler's late start to playing golf
quotes.excerpt: I never touched a golf club till I was 27 years old.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: I started playing last summer. I never touched a golf club till I was 27 years old. The only reason I did, and now I became addicted to it, but the only reason I did was because at the time the Phoenix Suns were owned by Carsten Pange of Pange Golf Club. They had a program in the league that as an opposing player coming into Phoenix, you could go out to the Pange factory and get custom fitted for clubs.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's late interest in golf
quotes.excerpt: LeBron took this up very late in regard to how most guys do it in their careers.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Legler
text_blocks.text: For LeBron, most dudes now they play golf. Even when we were interviewing Dylan Harper this morning, he is already playing. It is a normal thing that basketball players do now. So LeBron took this up very late in regard to how most guys do it in their careers, but he definitely seems like he has got the bug because I have seen a lot of videos of LeBron James on the golf course.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of evaluating players as a former star
quotes.excerpt: When you are that great at something, how do you go and evaluate a player?
quotes.quote: It is going to be hard to stay connected. We saw with Michael Jordan. Michael Jordan tried it. When you are that great at something, how do you go and evaluate a player? Because we all evaluate players through the lens we see the game. And for him, how does he evaluate a player through his lens and how he sees the game? It is similar to Shaquille O'Neal, right? If you listen to Shaquille O'Neal speak on TV, oftentimes you are like, I feel what you are saying, but it is so hard to do that, but you can.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: The challenge of LeBron James becoming a general manager
quotes.excerpt: I don't know how he does something like that, be the general manager of a team.
quotes.quote: I don't know how he does something like that, be the general manager of a team as the star that he is, the lens that he sees it through, and all the other things that he has going on to then take a job like that where you are in one place for, you know, I just I don't see it.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: The time commitment of being a front office executive
quotes.excerpt: You go take a job like that, if you are not fully committed every day, the phone's not turned off.
quotes.quote: You go take a job like that, if you are not fully committed every day, and that there is no really, you are not ever on downtime, the phone is not turned off when you are in a role like that. But at the same time, I feel like those guys, a lot of those guys, they have such a yearning desire to compete and be part of some in some way winning and losing.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Tim Legler coached AAU basketball
quotes.excerpt: I needed to contribute to winning and losing something. I just did.
quotes.quote: That is why I coached AAU basketball and the Under Armour circuit for years, because I needed to contribute to winning and losing something. I just did. Golf is great and all that, and I was playing it and it was fun, competitive and betting on every shot with your friends, there is nothing like putting a scoreboard up there and knowing you have something to do with it, the outcome.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's likely future path in NBA ownership
quotes.excerpt: I think the most likely path is probably ownership.
quotes.quote: I think the most likely path is probably ownership, right? Like you get into ownership and he is going to be one of those owners that have an opinion on what is happening with the team, right? But I think that has to be, like I said, look at Michael Jordan. Michael Jordan was so disgusted with other basketball players that he said, hey man, you know what, forget this job, I am going to just go play myself.

quotes.speaker: Draymond Green
quotes.summary_phrase: The difficulty of transitioning from player to coach
quotes.excerpt: Why didn't you get into head coach or general manager?
quotes.quote: Your knowledge for the game, which I spoke about at the top of the show, the way you view it, the way you teach it, why didn't you get into head coach or general manager? Especially, you know, we have seen guys now going from media and you get to understand their brain and you are like, holy shit man, this is a coach.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Why Tim Legler didn't pursue an NBA coaching career
quotes.excerpt: I was spending more time preparing my knee for practice than I was even practicing at that point.
quotes.quote: When I got out of the league, I did not know exactly what I wanted to do. I had a very serious knee injury and I had a couple more years of pay coming from the Golden State Warriors actually, was my last team I played for. I was spending more time preparing my knee for practice than I was even practicing at that point. And the post-practice stuff, it was wearing on me. I was not the same, I did not have the same lift, I was having a harder time getting open, I was wearing a brace, it was wearing me down.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler's post-playing career at Wharton
quotes.excerpt: I went to the executive program at Wharton.
quotes.quote: I went to the executive program at Wharton. I mean, I bit off a big one man. Yeah, exactly. So I could have just gone to business school and I am like, no, you know what, I am going to go to Wharton and go to the executive program at Wharton and I did that and I met incredible people in there like I knew I would.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: How an ESPN job changed Tim Legler's life
quotes.excerpt: I got this phone call from ESPN and coaching was always on my mind, by the way.
quotes.quote: Coaching was always on my mind, by the way, at that time. It was definitely on my mind, but I was so fresh out of the league, I kind of wanted to step away from basketball at the time, I was fried, mentally fried. And then that phone call came from ESPN and changed my life. They have seen you do some interviews, they like what you had to say and the way you articulate the game, do you want to come up for an audition?

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Balancing family life with an NBA broadcasting career
quotes.excerpt: The thing I loved about broadcast, I loved the job, I loved talking about the game.
quotes.quote: The thing I loved about broadcast, I loved the job, I loved talking about the game, I loved being connected to the league, I loved it pays well. The schedule was the thing that was so great. I am like, damn man, I get to literally be basically a full-time father and still be able to do this job in basketball connected to the game.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: Tim Legler's interviews for NBA coaching jobs
quotes.excerpt: I actually interviewed for several head division one coaching jobs about six, eight years ago.
quotes.quote: I actually interviewed for several head division one coaching jobs about six, eight years ago. I was like, okay, that is it. They grew up, both my kids gave me their blessing, Dad, you sacrificed so much for us, we know you wanted to coach, we are cool, we are good now, go do your thing. I was just not able to get the job, I could not get find that athletic director man to pull the trigger and hire me.

quotes.speaker: Tim Legler
quotes.summary_phrase: The impact of NIL and the transfer portal on college basketball
quotes.excerpt: That was right before NIL and the portal.
quotes.quote: That was right before NIL and the portal. And most college coaches I know now are like, this is a totally different landscape. This is not even the same job that they fell in love with. It is a very, very frustrating place to work.
